title: Give Me Some Feedback About My Feedback
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Opening with Ken Blanchard's line that feedback is 'the breakfast of champions,' this Field Note argues that leaders shouldn't just give feedback -- they should ask team members how the feedback itself lands, since delivery style heavily determines whether advice is accepted or resisted. Asking this meta-question signals that feedback is genuinely about the recipient's growth rather than the leader's agenda, and often surfaces issues of accuracy or timeliness the leader wasn't aware of. The piece frames this practice as a low-cost way for leaders to build a healthier appetite for feedback across the team.
points: Asking team members for feedback about how feedback itself is delivered is presented as a distinct, underused practice.
This meta-question signals the feedback process is about the recipient's growth, not the leader's agenda.
Team members' responses can surface issues of accuracy or timeliness the leader was unaware of.
Leaders are cautioned to listen and adapt to input rather than reacting defensively to it.
The practice is framed as recalibrating the relationship and building a healthier appetite for future feedback.
quotes: Feedback is the breakfast of champions.” But not everyone wants to eat that breakfast.
It’s not enough for leaders to simply offer the feedback team members need. Promoting a healthy appetite for feedback is the job of every good leader.
Leaders who are wise enough to ask this question increase the appetite for more feedback in the future.
Asking for feedback about feedback will also reveal issues of accuracy and timeliness.
It often recalibrates the relationship because it reinforces the leader’s positive intent. Just another bonus provided by a simple question.
